title: struct, class, and nested data types

spans.text: A `struct` groups related data under one name and can contain another `struct`, methods, or arrays of instances. The main language difference from `class` is default access: `struct` members are public by default; `class` members are private. Use a `struct` for simple sensor records and a `class` when data and invariants should be protected together.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: A `float` affects layout and size. Sending a structure as raw bytes is not portable: padding and byte order can differ between boards.
